title: Memory-Bound Edge Efficiency Envelope (MBEEE): A Hardware-Level Analytical Model
abstract_snippet:
Continuous edge inference introduces architectural constraints that extend beyond raw computational throughput. Sustained vision workloads expose the energetic and latency costs of data movement across heterogeneous memory hierarchies. In discrete CPU--GPU platforms, the cost of transferring data across the PCIe bus can approach---and occasionally exceed---the cost of the computation itself.

Skadron et al. b_thermal established thermal-aware microarchitectural design principles, highlighting the limits of frequency scaling under sustained load. We apply similar thermodynamic reasoning to continuous edge inference, focusing on steady-state rather than burst behavior.

Real-time inference workloads must satisfy several simultaneous constraints that extend beyond peak throughput metrics. Continuous workloads are bounded by latency deadlines, thermal stability, and available energy budgets. The MBEEE formalizes this joint constraint space.

The modeled advantages of unified memory assume specific analytical interactions between execution units and the underlying memory subsystem. Without tight integration, the expected gains do not fully materialize.

On UMA platforms, the analysis assumes zero-copy semantics. Instead of modeling a physical data copy, the tensor is mapped onto a shared physical memory space. The memory controller pinning prevents paging and exposes that address directly to the NPU or GPU execution engine.
